outcome_detail: The StreamingLLM kernel only adds the `n_init` attention sinks when the sequence is longer than the local window; for `k_len <= n_local` it runs a plain sliding-window attention with no sinks. The caller-supplied `n_init`/`n_local` therefore decide whether the sink mechanism is active at all.

The KV cache kept for subsequent decoding is either the full h_k/h_v (short context) or a concatenation of the first n_init keys and the last n_local keys (long context), changing what state later steps attend to.

In stream_llm_forward, len_k > n_local selects the two-stage path with RoPE-rotated init queries/keys over the first n_init positions; otherwise init_h_k/init_h_v are empty and only the local sliding-window attention is computed.
